Architectural Context: Operationalizing Butler Lampson's Confinement Laws & Multi-Domain Treaties (Provisional #2A)

In Butler Lampson's classic formulation of the Confinement Problem (Communications of the ACM, 1973)—later extended to AI boxing by Yampolskiy (Leakproofing the Singularity: Artificial Intelligence Confinement Problem, 2012)—confining an untrusted program requires four strict invariants: Total Isolation, Transitivity, Masking (controlling inputs to legitimate and covert channels), and Enforcement (trapping escape or probing attempts).

Passing raw enterprise, medical, or classified entity graphs into an external LLM or third-party embedding API violates Lampson's first two laws immediately: the external model becomes a transitive leakage channel. AINA's Semantic Switch (Provisional #2A) enforces confinement upstream of the model through a Fiction-First Pipeline paired with MX2MX Sovereign Boundary Governance:

Confinement & Multi-Agent ProblemClassical Failure Mode in Standard AI PipelinesAINA Semantic Switch & MX2MX Mechanism (Provisional #2A)
1. Transitive Leakage to External Models & Vector DBs (Lampson Laws 1 & 2: Isolation & Transitivity)Raw PII, proprietary schemas, or operational graphs are sent to external LLM APIs or stored as inverted embeddings in vector databases where they can be reconstructed.Fiction-First Pipeline & Chartered Target Fiction Domains (DomainCharterObject): Protected reality is never transmitted to an untrusted model. The Semantic Switch projects permitted structural relations into a chartered synthetic target domain using deterministic Relation IDs (RIDs) while preserving graph isomorphism (20/20 invariance blocks and 23/23 exact relations verified below).
2. Covert Channels, Timing Side-Channels & Active Probing (Lampson Laws 3 & 4: Masking & Enforcement)An adversarial or jailbroken agent probes restricted graph edges and infers redacted facts from error diffs, latency variations, or partial query returns.Constant-Time Anti-Knowledge Oracle (AKO) & Honeypot Traps: Forbidden relation classes are severed into a SeveranceAntiKnowledgeObject governed by an active Anti-Knowledge Oracle (AKO). To close oracle lookup-timing side channels under a bounded query budget, AKO evaluates batch admissibility in constant time (O(1) Bloom-filter + fixed-cycle lookup) with uniform refusal envelopes, and plants Anti-Knowledge Honeypots that immediately trap and revoke standing when an agent probes a forbidden relation path.
3. Exfiltration of Context Windows or Vector StoresIf an attacker dumps the prompt cache or vector database, they obtain actionable real-world records.Constitutional Inertness & Coupled Dual-Ledger State Machine: Semantic projection (Correspondence Ledger) is decoupled from execution authority (Standing Ledger). Without a live, hardware/kernel-bound Standing Ledger token, exfiltrated fiction-domain tokens are constitutionally inert and carry zero authority to mutate protected state.
4. Multi-Agent Value Alignment Across Competing Organizations (Yampolskiy's Personal Universes Problem)Expecting independent organizations, coalitions, or jurisdictions to agree on a single global alignment rubric or shared database schema is impossible.MX2MX Sovereign Treaties & Monotonic Burden Accumulator (MBA): Each organization operates inside its own sovereign chartered domain. When machine consequence crosses a boundary, MX2MX executes Dual Constitutional Re-binding under a cryptographic TreatyObject where authority strictly contracts (Sₙ₊₁ = Sₙ ∩ S_destination) and verification obligations accumulate monotonically (Bₙ₊₁ = Bₙ ∪ B_new).

Scope of Covert-Channel & Anonymization Claims: In accordance with Lampson's distinction between legitimate and covert channels, constant-time AKO evaluation (O(1) lookup + uniform refusal envelopes) specifically bounds oracle lookup-timing and error-diff side channels within a single query batch. It does not by itself eliminate external system side channels such as network packet-size correlation, shared-cache contention, or multi-query structural intersection attacks against known auxiliary graphs. The Stage-Zero fixtures below evaluate deterministic structural isomorphism (20/20 invariance blocks, 23/23 exact relations), not universal differential privacy.

Scope & Maturity Disclosure

Maturity & Scope Note: Unlike the core deterministic execution, lease-fencing, and server-cut provenance layers (§01, §02, §04–§08), the Semantic Switch is an early-stage experimental research module. The 20/20 block-invariance and 23/23 relation-preservation fixtures in this pack validate deterministic structural isomorphism on synthetic test vectors only; they do not claim production entity-resolution recall across arbitrary noisy text or universal cryptographic anonymity against auxiliary-data reconstruction attacks.

The primary public proof of the execution architecture is the Refusal & Conformance Proof Pack.

Engineering purpose: blind execution with relational structure intact

Semantic Switch is a deterministic relational confinement layer, not an encryption or anonymity system. It preserves equivalence relations, edit-distance structure, and graph topology so confined workers can perform entity-resolution tasks without receiving raw customer identifiers in their prompts. Frequency analysis, auxiliary-graph correlation, tokenizer-boundary effects, and production recall remain outside the proof ceiling.

A public, reproducible evidence bundle for relation-isomorphic protected computation. The fixtures are synthetic; no customer records, private crosswalk, credentials, native identifiers, local keys, or provider calls are included.

The pipeline being tested

The two input files describe the same relational object under different native relabelings. A correct generator must preserve the relational structure, not the native token identities. The relation audit separately requires every eligible native edit type to remain visible in the fictional representation.

Reproduce the evidence

  1. Obtain or build a Semantic Switch executable with the relation-isomorphism-v1 feature.
  2. Download verify.py and this pack's fixtures and harnesses.
  3. Run python verify.py --binary /path/to/semantic-switch.
  4. Compare the fresh JSON summary with the retained invariance result and exact-relation result.

The driver creates a temporary random local key, prepares both inputs, verifies every record and field, computes fresh reports, and deletes the temporary workspace. It exits successfully only when all 20 blocks and all 23 eligible relations pass.

Claim ceiling

These results establish deterministic transport fidelity, exact relation preservation, complete local verification, and adversarial restoration behavior on the declared synthetic fixtures. They do not establish anonymity, inference resistance, universal privacy, matching accuracy, production merge correctness, or independent validation of a customer population. Native rows, keys, and the private crosswalk remain under client control.
